_meta.indication: Treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 51 skipping; approved under accelerated approval based on an increase in dystrophin in skeletal muscle.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 1 (double-blind, placebo-controlled), followed by open-label extension Study 2; and Study 3 (Study 301)
pivotal_trials.phase: Not specified as a phase; approval was based primarily on a post hoc comparison of 12 treated DMD patients to 13 external untreated controls.
pivotal_trials.design: Study 1: 24-week double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial, then open-label extension Study 2 (up to 208 weeks) compared to an external control group; Study 3: open-label, 48-week single-arm study with paired baseline/Week 48 muscle biopsies.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene amenable to exon 51 skipping, on stable corticosteroids; mean age 9.4 years in Study 1 and 8.9 years in Study 3.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint in Study 1 was dystrophin production; the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) was assessed as a clinical outcome measure.
pivotal_trials.n: Study 1: 12 patients randomized (EXONDYS 51 30 mg/kg n=4, 50 mg/kg n=4, placebo n=4); Study 3: 13 patients treated, 12 evaluable.
pivotal_trials.result: No significant difference in 6MWD change between EXONDYS 51 and placebo. In Study 3, mean dystrophin was 0.16% of normal before treatment and 0.44% after 48 weeks (p < 0.05); median increase 0.1% (mean change p=0.008). In Study 2, average dystrophin was 0.93% of normal after 180 weeks and Study 2 failed to show clinical benefit vs the external control.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5% and higher than placebo) were balance disorder and vomiting. In Study 1, balance disorder occurred in 38% and vomiting in 38% of EXONDYS 51 patients (both 0% placebo), and contact dermatitis in 25% (0% placebo). Among 88 patients treated ≥30 mg/kg/week for up to 208 weeks, events in ≥10% and more frequent than in Study 1 included vomiting, contusion, excoriation, arthralgia, rash, catheter site pain, and upper respiratory tract infection.
target_moa: Eteplirsen binds to exon 51 of dystrophin pre-mRNA, causing exclusion of that exon during mRNA processing (exon skipping) so that an internally truncated but partially functional dystrophin protein can be produced in patients with mutations amenable to exon 51 skipping.
modality: Oligonucleotide — an antisense oligonucleotide of the phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) subclass.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was presented to the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee on April 25, 2016. On the key vote on whether substantial evidence showed eteplirsen induces dystrophin to a level reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, the vote was 5 YES, 8 NO, 0 ABSTAIN.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Increase in dystrophin in skeletal muscle (dystrophin production measured by Western blot) — a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

confirmatory_requirement.text: PMR 3095-1: a 2-year randomized, double-blind, controlled trial to verify the clinical benefit of eteplirsen in patients amenable to exon 51 skipping, comparing the approved 30 mg/kg weekly dosage to a higher-exposure regimen, with primary endpoint the North Star Ambulatory Assessment.

citations.quote: 3095-1 In order to verify the clinical benefit of etelprisen, conduct a 2-year randomized, double-blind, controlled trial of etelprisen in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 51 skipping. Patients should be randomized to the approved dosage of etelprisen (30 mg/kg weekly) or to a dosage that provides significantly higher exposure, e.g., 30 mg/kg daily. The primary endpoint will be the North Star Ambulatory Assessment.

orphan_indication.text: Eteplirsen is an orphan product; Duchenne muscular dystrophy is an orphan indication.

summary.text: EXONDYS 51 (eteplirsen), an orphan product for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, received accelerated approval on the basis of an increase in dystrophin in skeletal muscle (a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit), following a Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee meeting; continued approval is contingent on a required confirmatory trial (PMR 3095-1) to verify clinical benefit.
